London, 13<sup>th</sup> February 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Ridge Mining** is in discussions with larger rival Aquarius Platinum that could lead to a takeover offer being made for Ridge, the firm said on Thursday.  Shares in Ridge Mining leapt 50,8% on Thursday, to 47,5p by 16:20 in London.  However, the company cautioned that there was no certainty over the terms or structure of a potential transaction, nor that Aquarius and Ridge would come to an agreement. Aquarius CEO Stuart Murray said last week that he expected 2009 would prove a “year of consolidation” in South Africa’s platinum sector.  Aquarius posted a first half net loss of $70-million, and lowered its 2009 production target by 100 000 oz, to 475 000 oz.  Ridge Mining said previously that it expects to produce the first platinum concentrate from its Blue Ridge mine, in South Africa, at the end of this month.  In the last six months, two potential merger and acquisition transactions were abandoned because of volatile markets and the low pricing environment. 

## _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Northam Platinum CEO** Glyn Lewis says that the immediate outlook for the platinum market is uncertain.  “The recent turmoil in the auto- motive manufacturing industry injured the demand for platinum, rhodium and palladium,” he said in Johannesburg last week, adding that demand for PGMs from the industrial, electrical and chemicals sectors had contracted in the wake of the global recession.  However, the jewellery sector was now faced with opportunities for an increase in demand, as manufacturers and retailers sought to take advantage of lower, less volatile metal prices.  On the supply side, he noted, the sharp decline in PGM prices had led to producers reconsidering the timelines of the new projects they were contemplating.  Further, the volumes of metal derived from recycling had contracted significantly.  “There is no doubt that 2009 will provide a challenging market for PGM producers and shareholders alike; thereafter, we believe, the demand for our basket of metals will show some recovery. As such, we remain cautiously optimistic that prices will trend higher in 2010,” he added. 

## _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Toyota Motor Corp.** said Thursday night that it is freezing wage, reducing hours and adopting a voluntary exit program, and it is still refraining from laying off any North American workers.  The new measures, which Toyota dubbed a “shared sacrifice” philosophy, come as the automaker faces its first financial losses since 1950 and the unfamiliar specter of idle factory lines.  Toyota has gone out of its way to keep its mostly non-union U.S. and Canadian production workers on the clock, even as it has shut down assembly lines. But a statement released by Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America Inc., the company’s U.S. manufacturing headquarters, said there is now a “strong possibility” that it will reduce work and pay at some plants.Toyota is consider

ing a schedule in which some workers would work 72 hours in a typical 80-hour, two-week period. 

## _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Russians** bought 116,899 new cars in January, 33% less than a year earlier, according to monthly data released by the Association of European Businesses on Thursday.  The association, whose members include the heads of international car makers in Moscow, also cut its 2009 forecast for new car sales in the country to 1.9 million from 2.4 million.  That revision brings the association’s official forecast in line with what many executives have being saying for several weeks, and shows how tighter terms for car loans have again put purchases beyond the reach of millions of Russians.  As Europe’s mature market slowed down last year, international car makers pinned their hopes on Russia’s growing consumer base.
